summary: Director review of the revision-1 PR (#62) found four residual passages in src/content/lessons/lines/03-head-line.mdx that, while no longer matching the automated claim-risk heuristic's word list, still exceeded the approved evidence boundary: (1) line 42 'and it is one that is consistently read across the Western tradition' asserted unattributed cross-tradition reading consistency for path/slope; (2) line 48 'a moderate downward slope is a normal middle case' replaced a removed frequency claim with an unsupported population-norm/distribution claim; (3) line 72 'It comes to a clear terminus somewhere in the outer half of the palm' turned the prior removed 'In most hands...' wording into an effectively universal anatomical/prevalence claim, one that also contradicts the lesson's own Length section (line 64), which allows a head line to stop 'somewhere in the middle' or end 'noticeably earlier'; (4) line 68 'A short head line is a reading popular palmistry gets wrong' attributed a behavior/error to the vague, unattributed population 'popular palmistry'. All four were corrected: (1) reworded to the plain direct observation 'This is a clearly observable variable in the head line', dropping the consensus claim entirely; (2) reworded to 'simply falls between the two', a positional statement rather than a distribution/norm claim; (3) reworded to the neutral observation instruction 'Look at where your head line comes to its terminus', asserting no fixed location; (4) reworded to the direct, unattributed corrective statement 'A short head line does not, on its own, indicate limited intelligence', with the now-redundant adjacent 'simplistic gloss... is not what the careful tradition says' sentence removed as duplicative once the direct statement carries the correction (the sourced Benham/Gettings sentence immediately after is unchanged). None of the four replacements introduces an equivalent unsupported synonym (no 'normal', 'usual', 'standard', 'generally', or 'consistently' was reintroduced). No other revision-1 wording, lesson structure, figures, or learning flow were touched. Full claim-by-claim disposition recorded in docs/source-verification-log.md under a new revision-2 section; a matching revision-2 entry was added to docs/CHANGELOG.md directly above the existing PP-RELAY-040 entry, which is unchanged and remains accurate to what it describes (the revision-1 diff).

revision_2_findings_disposition.finding: line 42: 'one that is consistently read across the Western tradition'
revision_2_findings_disposition.detail: Unattributed cross-tradition consistency claim removed. Sentence now reads 'This is a clearly observable variable in the head line.' with no consensus claim of any kind.

revision_2_findings_disposition.finding: line 48: 'a moderate downward slope is a normal middle case'
revision_2_findings_disposition.detail: Unsupported norm/distribution wording replaced with the plain positional statement 'a moderate downward slope simply falls between the two'; no population-frequency or norm claim retained.

revision_2_findings_disposition.finding: line 72: 'It comes to a clear terminus somewhere in the outer half of the palm'
revision_2_findings_disposition.detail: Universalized endpoint-location claim removed. Sentence now reads 'Look at where your head line comes to its terminus.', asserting no fixed or majority location, consistent with the Length section's own allowance for lines ending earlier or in the middle.

revision_2_findings_disposition.finding: line 68: 'a reading popular palmistry gets wrong'
revision_2_findings_disposition.detail: Vague anonymous-population attribution removed. Sentence now states the corrective point directly and without attribution: 'A short head line does not, on its own, indicate limited intelligence.' The redundant adjacent sentence restating the same point via an unnamed 'simplistic gloss' was removed as duplicative; the sourced Benham/Gettings explanation immediately following is unchanged.
